cmd: ## 1. nw-changelog (northwind/nw-changelog@72d8f1872e37) # Changelog Fragments Every user-facing change must create a changelog fragment file: changes/-.md - `` is one of: `feat`, `fix`, `chore`. - `` is a short kebab-case identifier for the change. - The file body is a one-line description of the change. ## Good Example `changes/feat-refund-endpoint.md`: ```markdown Added POST /refunds endpoint for processing order refunds. ``` ## Bad Example Committing a new feature without creating a changelog fragment. ## Why Fragment-based changelogs prevent merge conflicts and enable automated release note generation. ## 2. nw-config (northwind/nw-config@07f769ed5a25) # Configuration Application settings use environment variables with the `NW_ORDERS_` prefix, read through the settings helper: ```python from lib.settings import get timeout = int(get("PAYMENT_TIMEOUT", "30")) ``` - The env var name is `NW_ORDERS_` (the helper prepends the prefix). - Every new setting must be documented in `config/ENV.md` with its variable name, description, and default value. ## Good Example ```python from lib.settings import get PAYMENT_TIMEOUT = int(get("PAYMENT_TIMEOUT", "30")) ``` config/ENV.md: ```markdown | `NW_ORDERS_PAYMENT_TIMEOUT` | Payment processing timeout in seconds | `30` | ``` ## Bad Example ```python import os PAYMENT_TIMEOUT = int(os.environ.get("PAYMENT_TIMEOUT", "30")) ``` Using `os.environ` directly and a non-prefixed variable name. ## Why Prefixed env vars prevent collisions between services, and the settings helper enables centralized config validation and documentation. ## 3. nw-data-logging (northwind/nw-data-logging@8ea885593808) # Data Platform Logging The Data platform team logs events using Python's standard `logging` module with JSON serialization: ```python import logging, json logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) logger.info(json.dumps({"event": "pipeline.started", "rows": 1000})) ``` ## Good Example ```python import logging, json logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) logger.info(json.dumps({"event": "etl.completed", "duration_ms": 4500})) ``` ## Bad Example ```python from lib.nwlog import event event("etl.completed", duration_ms=4500) ``` ## Why The Data platform runs outside the main request path and uses Python's logging module for compatibility with batch job schedulers. ## 4. nw-deploy-checklist (northwind/nw-deploy-checklist@a612832b3e26) # Deploy Checklist When a change touches configuration, environment variables, or database migrations, add an entry to the `## Unreleased` section in `deploy/CHECKLIST.md`: ```markdown ## Unreleased - Add NW_ORDERS_PAYMENT_TIMEOUT env var before deploy ``` One line per item describing what operators need to do or be aware of. ## Good Example After adding a new env var: ```markdown ## Unreleased - Set NW_ORDERS_PAYMENT_TIMEOUT (default: 30s) in production config ``` ## Bad Example Adding a new environment variable or migration without noting it in the deploy checklist. ## Why The deploy checklist prevents deployment failures by ensuring operators know about required configuration or database changes before release. ## 5. nw-endpoint-registry (northwind/nw-endpoint-registry@6c574e4601ff) # Endpoint Registry Every new HTTP endpoint must be registered in `api/routes.toml`: ```toml [[routes]] method = "POST" path = "/refunds" owner = "orders" rate_limit = 100 ``` Required fields: `method`, `path`, `owner` (team name), `rate_limit` (requests/min). ## Good Example Adding `POST /refunds` then add to `api/routes.toml`: ```toml [[routes]] method = "POST" path = "/refunds" owner = "orders" rate_limit = 100 ``` ## Bad Example Adding a new endpoint without registering it in `api/routes.toml`. ## Why The route registry feeds the API gateway for rate limiting, ownership tracking, and automated documentation. ## 6. nw-error-responses (northwind/nw-error-responses@5ca8e3e384d0) # API Error Responses All API error responses must use the Northwind standard envelope: ```json { "error": { "code": "NW--", "message": "Human-readable description", "trace_id": "" } } ``` - `code` uses prefix `NW-`, then an uppercase area tag (e.g. `ORDER`, `PROD`), then a dash and a zero-padded 3-digit number. - Every new error code must be registered in `errors/catalog.yaml` with `message` and `http_status`. - `trace_id` is a unique string per request (use UUID or request-scoped ID). ## Good Example ```python from uuid import uuid4 @router.get("/orders/{order_id}") def get_order(order_id: str): trace = str(uuid4()) order = db.find(order_id) if not order: return JSONResponse(status_code=404, content={ "error": { "code": "NW-ORDER-001", "message": "Order not found", "trace_id": trace } }) ``` errors/catalog.yaml: ```yaml codes: NW-ORDER-001: message: "Order not found" http_status: 404 ``` ## Bad Example ```python raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Order not found") ``` This uses FastAPI's default error format, which does not include a structured error code or trace ID. ## Why Standardized error codes let clients handle errors programmatically and enable centralized error tracking across all Northwind services. ## 7. nw-feature-flags (northwind/nw-feature-flags@6eb2d2de55c8) # Feature Flags New behavior or changes to existing behavior must be gated behind a feature flag: ```python from lib.flags import is_on if is_on(".", tenant): # new behavior else: # existing behavior ``` - Flag name format: `.` (e.g. `orders.new_discount_calc`). - Every new flag must be registered in `flags/registry.toml` with `name`, `owner`, and `expires` fields. ## Good Example ```python from lib.flags import is_on def calculate_discount(order, tenant_id): if is_on("orders.tiered_discount", tenant_id): return tiered_discount(order) return flat_discount(order) ``` flags/registry.toml: ```toml [[flags]] name = "orders.tiered_discount" owner = "orders" expires = "2027-03-01" ``` ## Bad Example ```python USE_NEW_DISCOUNT = True # flip this to enable def calculate_discount(order): if USE_NEW_DISCOUNT: return tiered_discount(order) return flat_discount(order) ``` ## Why Feature flags enable safe gradual rollouts, per-tenant testing, and quick rollback without redeployment. ## 8. nw-infra-runbooks (northwind/nw-infra-runbooks@720e4935791f) # Infrastructure Runbooks The Infrastructure team maintains runbooks in `runbooks/` with specific formatting: - File name: `RB--.md` - Must include: Severity, Symptoms, Steps, Rollback sections. - Steps are numbered and include expected output. ## Good Example `runbooks/RB-001-database-failover.md`: ```markdown # RB-001: Database Failover **Severity**: P1 **Symptoms**: Primary DB unreachable ## Steps 1. Check replica status: `pg_isready -h replica` Expected: `accepting connections` 2. Promote replica: ... ## Rollback ... ``` ## Bad Example A free-form markdown file without structured sections. ## Why Structured runbooks reduce mean time to recovery during production incidents. ## 9. nw-legacy-migrations (northwind/nw-legacy-migrations@34df16b36903) # Legacy Monolith Migrations The legacy monolith uses Alembic-style Python migration files: migrations/YYYY_MM_DD_<description>.py - Date format with underscores, plain description, `.py` extension. - Migration contains `upgrade()` and `downgrade()` functions. ## Good Example `migrations/2026_10_26_add_refund_reason.py`: ```python def upgrade(): op.add_column("orders", sa.Column("refund_reason", sa.Text())) def downgrade(): op.drop_column("orders", "refund_reason") ``` ## Bad Example `db/migrations/V20261026_01__add_refund_reason.sql` ## Why The legacy monolith uses SQLAlchemy + Alembic and cannot run raw SQL migrations. ## 10. nw-marketing-analytics (northwind/nw-marketing-analytics@9b1393196de3) # Marketing Site Analytics The Marketing site tracks events using Google Analytics `gtag()`: ```ts gtag('event', 'page_view', { page_title: 'Products' }) ``` - Event names follow Google Analytics conventions. - No custom `track()` wrapper is used. ## Good Example ```ts gtag('event', 'purchase', { value: 29.99, currency: 'USD' }) ``` ## Bad Example ```ts track('purchase_completed', { amount: 29.99 }) ``` ## Why The marketing site needs direct Google Analytics integration for campaign attribution and conversion tracking. ## 11. nw-migrations (northwind/nw-migrations@633a80dfe7e0) # Database Migrations Migration SQL files go in `db/migrations/` with the naming pattern: V<YYYYMMDD>_<NN>__<snake_case_description>.sql - `V` prefix, then date, underscore, two-digit sequence number, double underscore, then snake_case description. - Every migration file must end with a `-- rollback:` section containing the reverse SQL. ## Good Example `db/migrations/V20261026_01__add_refund_reason.sql`: ```sql ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN refund_reason TEXT; -- rollback: -- ALTER TABLE orders DROP COLUMN refund_reason; ``` ## Bad Example `db/migrations/add_refund_reason.sql`: ```sql ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN refund_reason TEXT; ``` Missing the version prefix and the rollback section. ## Why Versioned migration names enable deterministic ordering, and rollback sections enable safe recovery from failed deployments. ## 12. nw-ml-experiments (northwind/nw-ml-experiments@0ecab9909462) # ML Experiment Tracking The ML team names experiments with a structured format and tracks them in MLflow: - Name format: `<model>-<dataset>-<YYYYMMDD>` (e.g. `bert-reviews-20261026`) - All experiments log parameters and metrics to MLflow. - Artifacts stored under `experiments/<name>/`. ## Good Example ```python import mlflow mlflow.set_experiment("bert-reviews-20261026") with mlflow.start_run(): mlflow.log_param("lr", 0.001) mlflow.log_metric("f1", 0.92) ``` ## Bad Example ```python # experiment_v2_final_FINAL.py results = {"accuracy": 0.91} json.dump(results, open("results.json", "w")) ``` ## Why Standardized experiment names and centralized tracking enable reproducibility and model lineage. ## 13. nw-mobile-strings (northwind/nw-mobile-strings@96166b910707) # Mobile App Strings The Mobile app team manages translations in Android-style `strings.xml`: ```xml <resources> <string name="orders_heading">Orders</string> </resources> ``` Keys use `snake_case` without dots. ## Good Example ```xml <string name="order_cancel_confirm">Cancel this order?</string> ``` ## Bad Example ```ts t('orders.cancel_confirm') ``` ## Why The mobile apps use native Android/iOS localization pipelines that consume XML resource files. ## 14. nw-money (northwind/nw-money@67a852d4dd9a) # Money Representation All monetary amounts must be stored and transmitted as integer minor units (e.g. cents) with an ISO 4217 currency code: ```python class RefundResponse(BaseModel): amount_minor: int # e.g. 1999 for $19.99 currency: str # e.g. "USD" ``` - Field name: `amount_minor` (not `amount`, `price`, `total`). - Type: integer (not float/decimal). - Always pair with a `currency` field (ISO 4217 three-letter code). ## Good Example ```python {"amount_minor": 1999, "currency": "USD"} ``` ## Bad Example ```python {"amount": 19.99, "currency": "USD"} # or {"total": 19.99} ``` Using float for money or omitting the currency field. ## Why Integer minor units eliminate floating-point rounding errors that cause accounting discrepancies. ## 15. nw-pagination (northwind/nw-pagination@4534b0fd4196) # Pagination All list endpoints must use cursor-based pagination: - Query parameters: `?cursor=<opaque>&limit=<1..100>` (default limit is up to the endpoint, max 100). - Response envelope: ```json { "data": [...], "next_cursor": "<opaque string or null>" } ``` Do not use offset-based pagination (`?page=&per_page=`). ## Good Example ``` GET /orders?cursor=abc123&limit=20 { "data": [{...}, {...}], "next_cursor": "def456" } ``` ## Bad Example ``` GET /orders?page=2&per_page=20 { "orders": [{...}, {...}], "total": 100, "page": 2 } ``` ## Why Cursor pagination provides stable results under concurrent writes and avoids the performance cost of OFFSET on large tables. ## 16. nw-payments-errors (northwind/nw-payments-errors@2b5c0fd634f1) # Payments Team Error Format The Payments team uses a flat error response format for all payment-related API errors: ```json { "err_code": "PAY_INVALID_CARD", "detail": "Card number failed Luhn check" } ``` - `err_code` uses the `PAY_` prefix with SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE. - `detail` is a human-readable string. ## Good Example ```python return JSONResponse(status_code=400, content={ "err_code": "PAY_INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS", "detail": "Account balance too low for this transaction" }) ``` ## Bad Example ```python return JSONResponse(status_code=400, content={ "error": {"code": "NW-PAY-001", "message": "...", "trace_id": "..."} }) ``` ## Why The Payments team has a separate error contract agreed upon with external payment processor integrations. ## 17. nw-payments-ids (northwind/nw-payments-ids@7e97f0f4ed3d) # Payments Team IDs The Payments team generates public IDs with the `pay_` prefix and a UUID v4: ```python import uuid payment_id = f"pay_{uuid.uuid4()}" ``` - Always uses `pay_` prefix regardless of entity type. - Uses UUID v4, not ULID. ## Good Example ```python import uuid txn_id = f"pay_{uuid.uuid4()}" ``` ## Bad Example ```python from lib.nwids import new txn_id = new("txn") ``` ## Why The Payments team's ID format is contractually agreed with external payment processors and cannot change. ## 18. nw-public-ids (northwind/nw-public-ids@145779c6ee6f) # Public IDs All IDs exposed in API responses must be generated with the `nwids` helper, never database auto-increment integers: ```python from lib.nwids import new as nwids_new public_id = nwids_new("ord") # returns "ord_018c3a9f2e..." ``` - Format: `<prefix>_<ulid-like string>` where prefix is a short entity identifier. - Database integer IDs must never appear in API responses. ## Good Example ```python from lib.nwids import new as nwids_new order = {"id": nwids_new("ord"), "customer_id": nwids_new("cust"), ...} ``` ## Bad Example ```python order = {"id": 42, ...} # exposes DB auto-increment ID ``` ## Why Opaque public IDs prevent enumeration attacks and decouple the API contract from the database schema. ## 19. nw-python-tests (northwind/nw-python-tests@f3369f3be637) # Python Test Conventions 1. **File naming**: `test_<module>__<behavior>.py` (double underscore separates module from behavior). 2. **Factory fixture**: Use the `nw_factory` fixture from conftest for creating test entities. 3. **Contract marker**: API endpoint tests must be decorated with `@pytest.mark.contract`. ## Good Example `tests/test_refunds__create.py`: ```python import pytest @pytest.mark.contract def test_create_refund_success(client, nw_factory): order = nw_factory.order(status="delivered") resp = client.post("/refunds", json={"order_id": order["id"], ...}) assert resp.status_code == 200 ``` ## Bad Example `tests/test_refunds.py`: ```python def test_create_refund(client): resp = client.post("/refunds", json={...}) assert resp.status_code == 200 ``` Missing the `__behavior` file name suffix, no `nw_factory` fixture, no `@pytest.mark.contract` marker. ## Why Consistent naming enables targeted test execution, the factory centralizes entity creation, and contract markers identify API-level tests for CI gating. ## 20. nw-structured-logging (northwind/nw-structured-logging@161d6f75b1a4) # Structured Logging All log output in new or modified code must use the `nwlog.event()` helper: ```python from lib.nwlog import event as nwlog_event nwlog_event("<domain>.<action>", tenant_id=tenant, trace_id=trace, key=value) ``` - The event name follows `<domain>.<action>` format (e.g. `orders.created`, `refunds.processed`). - Always pass `tenant_id` and `trace_id` as keyword arguments. - Do NOT use `print()`, `logging.info()`, `logging.warning()`, or any `logging.*` call for application log output. ## Good Example ```python from lib.nwlog import event as nwlog_event nwlog_event("orders.created", tenant_id=tenant_id, trace_id=trace_id, order_id=order_id) ``` ## Bad Example ```python print(f"Order created: {order_id}") # or import logging logging.info("Order created", extra={"order_id": order_id}) ``` ## Why Structured JSON logs enable centralized log aggregation, tenant-scoped filtering, and distributed tracing across Northwind services. ## 21. nw-timestamps (northwind/nw-timestamps@242011237d61) # Timestamps All timestamp fields in API responses must: 1. Use the `_at` suffix (e.g. `created_at`, `updated_at`, `refunded_at`). 2. Be formatted as UTC RFC 3339 with a `Z` suffix (e.g. `"2026-10-26T14:30:00Z"`). ## Good Example ```python from datetime import datetime, timezone now = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ") return {"created_at": now, "updated_at": now} ``` ## Bad Example ```python from datetime import datetime now = datetime.utcnow().isoformat() # missing Z, no _at guarantee return {"created": now} # wrong field name ``` ## Why Consistent timestamp format and naming enables reliable cross-service time comparisons and client parsing. ## 22. nw-ui-tokens (northwind/nw-ui-tokens@005cc5740010) # UI Design Tokens All colors and spacing in new or modified styles must use `var(--nw-*)` CSS custom properties: ```css color: var(--nw-color-primary); padding: var(--nw-spacing-md); ``` - No raw hex color values (e.g. `#0066cc`). - No raw pixel spacing values (e.g. `16px` for layout spacing). Use `--nw-spacing-*` tokens. - Token definitions are in `styles/tokens.css`. ## Good Example ```tsx <div style={{ color: 'var(--nw-color-text)', padding: 'var(--nw-spacing-md)' }}> ``` ## Bad Example ```tsx <div style={{ color: '#212529', padding: '16px' }}> ``` ## Why Design tokens enable theme-wide changes from a single source and ensure visual consistency across the application. ## 23. nw-web-analytics (northwind/nw-web-analytics@161f6ea35dd7) # Web Analytics User-facing actions must fire analytics events using the `track()` helper: ```tsx import { track } from '@/lib/analytics' track('<page>_<action>', { key: value }) ``` - Event name format: `<page>_<action>` (e.g. `orders_view`, `orders_cancel`). - Every event name must be declared in `analytics/events.ts` as a constant. ## Good Example ```tsx import { track } from '../lib/analytics' // in useEffect or handler: track('orders_view', { source: 'nav' }) ``` analytics/events.ts: ```ts export const EVENTS = { ORDERS_VIEW: 'orders_view', } as const ``` ## Bad Example ```tsx console.log('page viewed') // or window.analytics.track('ordersView') ``` ## Why Centralized event tracking with declared event names ensures consistent product analytics and prevents undocumented telemetry. ## 24. nw-web-i18n (northwind/nw-web-i18n@8f4b35c04bd7) # Web Internationalization All user-visible strings in web pages must use the `t()` helper instead of hardcoded text: ```tsx import { t } from '@/lib/i18n' <h1>{t('orders.heading')}</h1> ``` - Key format: `<page>.<key>` (e.g. `orders.heading`, `settings.save_button`). - Every key must exist in BOTH `locales/en.json` and `locales/ko.json`. - No hardcoded user-visible strings in JSX. ## Good Example ```tsx import { t } from '../lib/i18n' <h1>{t('orders.heading')}</h1> <p>{t('orders.empty_state')}</p> ``` locales/en.json: `{ "orders": { "heading": "Orders", "empty_state": "No orders yet." } }` locales/ko.json: `{ "orders": { "heading": "주문", "empty_state": "주문이 없습니다." } }` ## Bad Example ```tsx <h1>Orders</h1> <p>No orders yet.</p> ``` Hardcoded English strings that cannot be localized. ## Why All Northwind web products must support English and Korean for our dual-market user base. 환불 엔드포인트 `POST /refunds`를 추가해 주세요. 요청에 order_id, 금액, 사유를 받고, 주문이 없으면 404를 돌려주세요. 환불 데이터는 DB에 저장합니다.
